set -euo pipefail

if [ -z "${PR_NUMBER}" ]; then
  echo "No PR number — skipping auto-approve."
  exit 0
fi

# Check which checkboxes are ticked.
# Auto-approve is enabled when EITHER:
#   1. `- [x] auto-approve-workflows` is checked (explicit approval, always approve)
#   2. `- [x] copilot-agent-session-done.yml` is checked (WEC pre-approval)
#      The WEC checkbox IS the maintainer's pre-approval — checking it means "run
#      this workflow and approve whatever it needs", eliminating the
#      "This workflow is awaiting approval from a maintainer" gate.
PR_BODY=$(gh pr view "${PR_NUMBER}" \
  --repo "${REPO}" \
  --json body -q '.body // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

AUTO_APPROVE_CHECKED=0
SESSION_DONE_CHECKED=0
printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" | grep -qiE '^\-\s*\[x\]\s*auto-approve-workflows' && AUTO_APPROVE_CHECKED=1 || true
printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" | grep -qiE '^\-\s*\[x\]\s*copilot-agent-session-done\.yml' && SESSION_DONE_CHECKED=1 || true

if [ "$AUTO_APPROVE_CHECKED" = "0" ] && [ "$SESSION_DONE_CHECKED" = "0" ]; then
  echo "⚡ Neither auto-approve-workflows nor copilot-agent-session-done.yml is checked — skipping."
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$AUTO_APPROVE_CHECKED" = "1" ]; then
  echo "⚡ auto-approve-workflows is CHECKED — approving pending runs for SHA ${HEAD_SHA:0:12}..."
else
  echo "⚡ copilot-agent-session-done.yml WEC checkbox is CHECKED (pre-approval) — auto-approving pending runs for SHA ${HEAD_SHA:0:12}..."
fi

# Fetch all workflow runs for this commit that require approval
PENDING_RUNS=$(gh api \
  "repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?head_sha=${HEAD_SHA}&status=action_required&per_page=100" \
  --jq '.workflow_runs[].id' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

if [ -z "$PENDING_RUNS" ]; then
  echo "✅ No pending workflow runs requiring approval for SHA ${HEAD_SHA:0:12}."
  printf '### ⚡ Auto-Approve\n\nNo action_required runs found for commit `%s`.\n' "${HEAD_SHA:0:12}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  exit 0
fi

APPROVED=0
FAILED=0
SUMMARY_LINES=""

while IFS= read -r RUN_ID; do
  [ -z "$RUN_ID" ] && continue
  RUN_NAME=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}" --jq '.name // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  if gh api --method POST "repos/${REPO}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}/approve" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ✅ Approved run #${RUN_ID} (${RUN_NAME})"
    APPROVED=$((APPROVED + 1))
    SUMMARY_LINES="${SUMMARY_LINES}\n- ✅ Run [#${RUN_ID}](https://github.com/${REPO}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}) — ${RUN_NAME}"
  else
    echo "  ⚠️  Failed to approve run #${RUN_ID} (${RUN_NAME}) — may require owner approval"
    FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
    SUMMARY_LINES="${SUMMARY_LINES}\n- ⚠️ Run [#${RUN_ID}](https://github.com/${REPO}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}) — ${RUN_NAME} (approval failed)"
  fi
done <<< "$PENDING_RUNS"

printf '### ⚡ Auto-Approve Results\n\n**Approved:** %d | **Failed:** %d\n%b\n' \
  "$APPROVED" "$FAILED" "$SUMMARY_LINES" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

if [ "$APPROVED" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ Auto-approved ${APPROVED} pending workflow run(s) for PR #${PR_NUMBER}."
fi
if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "⚠️  ${FAILED} run(s) could not be approved — owner approval may be required."
fi
run_commands.name: Approve all action_required workflow runs for head SHA

run_commands.command:
# ── 1. Decide whether to escalate ─────────────────────────────────
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
  # Nightly sweep — always run
  CAT="nightly_health_sweep"
  echo "escalate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "category=${CAT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
  echo "escalate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  CAT="${INPUT_CATEGORY:-general}"
  echo "category=${CAT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
elif [ "${CONCLUSION}" != "failure" ] && [ "${CONCLUSION}" != "timed_out" ]; then
  echo "escalate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "category=no_failure" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "✅ Workflow concluded with '${CONCLUSION}' — no escalation needed"
  exit 0
else
  echo "escalate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  # Auto-detect category from workflow name
  if echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "security\|codeql\|cve"; then
    CAT="security_alert"
  elif echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "mypy\|type"; then
    CAT="type_error"
  elif echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "coverage\|rag"; then
    CAT="coverage_regression"
  elif echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "lint\|ruff\|deferral"; then
    CAT="lint_failure"
  elif echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "pattern\|ci.pattern"; then
    CAT="ci_pattern"
  elif echo "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" | grep -qi "test\|pytest"; then
    CAT="test_failure"
  else
    CAT="general"
  fi
  echo "category=${CAT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

# ── 2. Resolve PR number ───────────────────────────────────────────
if [ "${INPUT_PR}" != "" ]; then
  PR_NUMBER="${INPUT_PR}"
else
  PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list \
    --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
    --head "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
    --state open \
    --json number \
    -q '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
fi

echo "pr_number=${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "head_branch=${HEAD_BRANCH}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "run_url=${RUN_URL}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "workflow_name=${WORKFLOW_NAME}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "ℹ️  Category: ${CAT} | PR: ${PR_NUMBER:-none} | Branch: ${HEAD_BRANCH}"

run_commands.command:
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
RUN_LINK="${RUN_URL:-https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions}"
OUT="${RUNNER_TEMP}/copilot_prompt.txt"
HDR="Session S${SESSION} | Branch: \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\` | Run: [${RUN_ID:-manual}](${RUN_LINK})"

# Build category-specific prompt using printf to avoid YAML multi-line string issues.
# All prompt content is written line-by-line to ${OUT}; no multi-line bash strings used.
case "${CATEGORY}" in
  test_failure)
    printf '@copilot Fix the failing tests in workflow **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Retrieve job logs via GitHub MCP tools to identify the exact failing tests\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Diagnose root cause (import errors, fixture issues, regressions, missing deps)\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Apply the minimal targeted fix -- do NOT remove or skip tests\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Run `python3 -m ruff check` and verify `python3 -m pytest <module> -x` passes\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md` with session entry\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Push fix and verify CI goes green\n\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Follow `.codex/CODEBASE_AGENCY_POLICY.md` -- leave codebase better than found.' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  lint_failure)
    printf '@copilot Fix the linting/style failures in workflow **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Run `python3 -m ruff check --statistics` to list all violations\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Run `python3 -m ruff check --fix` to auto-fix fixable issues\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Apply manual fixes for remaining violations\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Verify `python3 -m ruff check` exits 0\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Push -- do NOT disable rules or add noqa without justification\n\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Verify `scripts/ci/check_deferral_language.py` passes.' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  coverage_regression)
    printf '@copilot Fix the coverage regression detected by **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Check coverage.xml or workflow logs to identify modules that dropped\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Write targeted tests for the uncovered lines/branches\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Run `python3 -m pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` to verify\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Ensure coverage meets threshold in `.github/workflows/test-rag.yml` (>=30%%)\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Push fix' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  security_alert)
    printf '@copilot Remediate the security alerts detected by **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Use GitHub MCP tools to list all open CodeQL/secret-scanning/Dependabot alerts\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Triage by severity -- fix CRITICAL and HIGH alerts first\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Apply minimal safe fix per alert; verify no regressions\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. For dependency vulnerabilities: bump to patched version in pyproject.toml\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Add a Security Summary to `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Push fix -- CodeQL will re-scan on the new commit' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  type_error)
    printf '@copilot Fix the mypy/type-checking failures in **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Retrieve logs to identify exact mypy errors (file:line, error code)\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Fix each error -- use Optional, cast, or proper annotations\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Do NOT add new `# type: ignore` unless absolutely unavoidable\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Run `python3 -m mypy src/ --no-error-summary` to verify clean output\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Push fix' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  ci_pattern)
    printf '@copilot The CI Pattern Pipeline strict gate failed in **%s**.\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" > "${OUT}"
    printf '%s\n\n' "${HDR}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Run `python3 scripts/ci/ci_pattern_pipeline.py --check-only --strict` locally\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Review high-recurrence patterns flagged (see pattern DB)\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Apply `python3 scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py` for auto-fixable patterns\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. For manual patterns: trace root cause and apply targeted fix\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Run pipeline again to confirm it passes\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '7. Push fix' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  nightly_health_sweep)
    printf '@copilot Perform the nightly codebase health sweep (S%s).\n\n' "${SESSION}" > "${OUT}"
    printf 'Timestamp: %s | Branch: `%s`\n\n' "${TIMESTAMP}" "${HEAD_BRANCH}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Health-sweep checklist:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Run `python3 -m ruff check` -- fix any new violations\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Run `python3 scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py --check-only` -- fix auto-fixable\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Check GitHub for new open CodeQL alerts -- remediate CRITICAL/HIGH\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Verify `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md` updated in last 48h\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Review last 5 CI runs on `%s` for recurring failures\n' "${HEAD_BRANCH}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf '6. Update cognitive brain metadata if new patterns observed\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '7. Push any fixes with descriptive commit messages' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
  *)
    printf '@copilot Continue iterative self-healing for branch `%s`.\n\n' "${HEAD_BRANCH}" > "${OUT}"
    printf 'Workflow: %s | Run: [%s](%s)\n\n' "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" "${RUN_ID:-manual}" "${RUN_LINK}" >> "${OUT}"
    printf 'Steps required:\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '1. Review the failing workflow logs via GitHub MCP tools\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '2. Identify and fix root cause per `.codex/CODEBASE_AGENCY_POLICY.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '3. Run `python3 -m ruff check` and `python3 -m pytest -x` to verify\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '4. Update `docs/accountability/.codex/archive/reports/AGENT_ACCOUNTABILITY_REPORT.md`\n' >> "${OUT}"
    printf '5. Push fix -- leave the codebase better than found' >> "${OUT}"
    ;;
esac

run_commands.command:
# ── Rate-limit dedup guard: skip if ANY @copilot rescue/escalation/healing
# comment was posted < 30 min ago — unified across all three posting workflows
# (ci-rescue.yml, iterative-self-healing-ci.yml, copilot-iterative-self-healing.yml).
# Previously each workflow only checked its own marker, allowing all three
# to fire simultaneously for the same failure and each summon the agent
# independently.  The shared check ensures the first poster wins and the
# others are silenced for the 30-minute cooldown window.
SHA_SHORT="${HEAD_SHA:0:12}"
MARKER="<!-- copilot-healing:${SHA_SHORT}:${CATEGORY} -->"
JQ_EXPR='[.[] | select(.body | test("<!-- (ci-rescue-sha|copilot-escalation|copilot-healing):"))] | last | .created_at // empty'
LAST_POST=$(gh api \
  "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments?per_page=100" \
  --jq "$JQ_EXPR" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [ -n "$LAST_POST" ]; then
  NOW_TS=$(date +%s)
  LAST_TS=$(date -d "${LAST_POST}" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  ELAPSED=$(( NOW_TS - LAST_TS ))
  if [ "$ELAPSED" -lt 1800 ]; then
    echo "::notice::Skipping copilot-healing prompt — a rescue/escalation/healing comment was already posted ${ELAPSED}s ago (< 30 min cooldown)"
    echo "### ⏭️ @copilot Prompt Skipped (cooldown — shared marker)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "An @copilot escalation was already posted ${ELAPSED}s ago. Cooldown: 1800s." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Build body via run-ID-unique temp file (TEMPORARY_FILES_POLICY.md) to
# avoid collisions when parallel jobs run on the same runner.
BODY_FILE="${RUNNER_TEMP}/copilot_healing_body_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}.txt"
{
  printf '%s\n' "${MARKER}"
  cat "${PROMPT_FILE}"
  printf '\n---\n_[🔗 Workflow run](https://github.com/%s/actions/runs/%s)_\n' \
    "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
} > "${BODY_FILE}"

# Paginate through ALL PR comments to find the existing upsert marker.
# PRs with >100 comments require pagination; a single page=1&per_page=100
# would miss comments on later pages, silently creating a duplicate.
# Cap at MAX_PAGES to prevent unbounded API calls on very large PRs.
EXISTING_ID=""
PAGE=1
MAX_PAGES=50
while [ -z "${EXISTING_ID}" ] && [ "${PAGE}" -le "${MAX_PAGES}" ]; do
  BATCH=$(gh api \
    "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments?per_page=100&page=${PAGE}" \
    --jq ".[] | select(.body | contains(\"${MARKER}\")) | .id" \
    2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "${BATCH}" ]; then
    EXISTING_ID=$(echo "${BATCH}" | head -1)
    break
  fi
  # Stop if the last page returned fewer than 100 entries (no more pages).
  COUNT=$(gh api \
    "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments?per_page=100&page=${PAGE}" \
    --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  [ "${COUNT}" -lt 100 ] && break
  PAGE=$((PAGE + 1))
done
if [ -z "${EXISTING_ID}" ] && [ "${PAGE}" -gt "${MAX_PAGES}" ]; then
  echo "⚠️  Reached max page limit (${MAX_PAGES}) searching for existing prompt comment; will create new."
fi

if [ -n "${EXISTING_ID}" ]; then
  # Update in-place; surface error if PATCH fails so CI shows failure.
  gh api --method PATCH \
    "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${EXISTING_ID}" \
    --field "body=@${BODY_FILE}" \
    || { echo "❌ Failed to update comment #${EXISTING_ID}"; exit 1; }
  echo "✅ Updated existing @copilot prompt (comment #${EXISTING_ID}) on PR #${PR_NUMBER}"
  echo "### ✅ @copilot prompt updated on PR #${PR_NUMBER} (comment #${EXISTING_ID})" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
else
  gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" \
    --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
    --body-file "${BODY_FILE}"
  echo "✅ Posted @copilot self-healing prompt on PR #${PR_NUMBER}"
  echo "### ✅ @copilot prompt posted on PR #${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi
run_commands.name: Upsert @copilot prompt as PR comment

run_commands.command:

  && echo "✅ Remote branch refs fetched (as origin/*)" \
  || echo "⚠️ Remote ref fetch failed (non-blocking)"
git branch -f main origin/main 2>/dev/null \
  && echo "✅ main available as local branch ref" \
  || echo "⚠️ Could not create local main ref (non-blocking)"
BASE="${{ github.base_ref }}"
if [ -n "$BASE" ] && [ "$BASE" != "main" ]; then
  git branch -f "$BASE" "origin/$BASE" 2>/dev/null \
    && echo "✅ $BASE available as local branch ref" \
    || echo "⚠️ Could not create local $BASE ref (non-blocking)"
fi
run_commands.name: 🔀 Fetch remote branch refs for PR diff support

run_commands.command:
echo "── §0.4: Inspecting PR for merge conflicts ──"
BASE="${BASE_REF}"

if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
  MERGEABLE=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json mergeable -q .mergeable 2>/dev/null || echo "UNKNOWN")
  echo "PR #${PR_NUMBER} mergeable status: ${MERGEABLE}"
  if [ "$MERGEABLE" = "CONFLICTING" ]; then
    echo "::warning::§0.4 MERGE CONFLICT DETECTED — PR #${PR_NUMBER}"
    echo "  has merge conflicts with base branch '${BASE}'."
    echo "  Agent MUST resolve these before any other work."
    echo "COPILOT_MERGE_CONFLICT=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  elif [ "$MERGEABLE" = "MERGEABLE" ]; then
    echo "✅ No merge conflicts detected"
    echo "COPILOT_MERGE_CONFLICT=false" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  else
    echo "ℹ️ Mergeable status: ${MERGEABLE} (GitHub may still be computing)"
    echo "COPILOT_MERGE_CONFLICT=unknown" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  fi
fi

if [ -n "$BASE" ]; then
  BEHIND=$(git rev-list --count "HEAD..origin/${BASE}" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  AHEAD=$(git rev-list --count "origin/${BASE}..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  echo "Branch status: ${BEHIND} behind, ${AHEAD} ahead of ${BASE}"
  if [ "$BEHIND" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::warning::§0.4 BRANCH DIVERGED — Branch is ${BEHIND}"
    echo "  commit(s) behind '${BASE}'."
    echo "  Agent should rebase or merge base before starting work."
    echo "COPILOT_BRANCH_BEHIND=${BEHIND}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  else
    echo "✅ Branch is up-to-date with ${BASE}"
    echo "COPILOT_BRANCH_BEHIND=0" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  fi
fi

if [ -n "$BASE" ] && git rev-parse "origin/${BASE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  MERGE_BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD "origin/${BASE}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$MERGE_BASE" ]; then
    CONFLICT_FILES=$(git merge-tree "$MERGE_BASE" HEAD "origin/${BASE}" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<<<<<<< ' || echo "0")
    if [ "$CONFLICT_FILES" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "::warning::§0.4 POTENTIAL CONFLICTS — merge-tree detected ${CONFLICT_FILES} file(s) with conflicts against '${BASE}'"
    else
      echo "✅ merge-tree: no file-level conflicts detected"
    fi
  fi
fi

echo "── §0.4 merge conflict pre-check complete ──"
run_commands.name: 🔀 Merge Conflict Pre-Check (session start)

run_commands.command:
echo "── §0.2: Checking for open CI failure report issues ──"
REPO="Aries-Serpent/_codex_"

CI_FAILURES=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label "ci-failure" --state open \
  --json number,title,updatedAt --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
echo "Open ci-failure issues: ${CI_FAILURES}"

HEALTH_ALERTS=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label "ci-health-alert" --state open \
  --json number,title,updatedAt --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
echo "Open ci-health-alert issues: ${HEALTH_ALERTS}"

TOTAL=$((CI_FAILURES + HEALTH_ALERTS))
echo "COPILOT_CI_FAILURE_ISSUES=${TOTAL}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

if [ "$TOTAL" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::§0.2 OPEN CI FAILURE ISSUES — ${TOTAL} open issue(s)"
  echo "  found (${CI_FAILURES} ci-failure, ${HEALTH_ALERTS} ci-health-alert)."
  echo "  Agent should review these for patterns affecting this PR."
  echo ""
  echo "── Open CI failure issues: ──"
  gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label "ci-failure" --state open \
    --json number,title --jq '.[] | "#\(.number): \(.title)"' 2>/dev/null || true
  gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label "ci-health-alert" --state open \
    --json number,title --jq '.[] | "#\(.number): \(.title)"' 2>/dev/null || true
else
  echo "✅ No open CI failure report issues"
fi

echo "── §0.2 CI failure issue check complete ──"
run_commands.name: 🚨 CI Failure Issue Check (session start)

run_commands.command:
echo "── Validating JSON files in .codex/ and docs/ ──"
FAIL=0
INVALID_FILES=""

while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  if ! python3 -m json.tool "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "::warning file=${f}::Invalid JSON detected (non-blocking): ${f}"
    INVALID_FILES="${INVALID_FILES}${f}\n"
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  fi
done < <(find .codex docs -name "*.json" -not -path "*/__pycache__/*" -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::⚠️ Found ${FAIL} invalid JSON file(s) — these will be addressed by agent session"
  echo "--- Invalid JSON Files ---"
  printf '%s' "$INVALID_FILES"

else

fi

run_commands.command:
if [ ! -f cognitive_app/src/server/cli_api_server.py ]; then
  echo "⚠️ cli_api_server.py not found — skipping (non-blocking)"
  exit 0
fi
pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx ptyprocess --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
# Explicitly forward auth tokens to the server process env.
# Even though CODEX_MASTER_KEY is in the job env block, child processes
# started with nohup inherit from the CURRENT step env — which already
# has these values. The explicit assignment below makes the intent clear
# and is idempotent.
export CODEX_MASTER_KEY="${CODEX_MASTER_KEY:-}"
export CODEX_BACKUP_KEY="${CODEX_BACKUP_KEY:-}"
export AGENT_GITHUB_TOKEN="${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}"
nohup uvicorn cognitive_app.src.server.cli_api_server:app \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8765 \
  --log-level warning \
  > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cli_api_server.log" 2>&1 &
CLI_API_PID=$!
echo "CLI_API_SERVER_PID=${CLI_API_PID}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
# Always export http://localhost:8765 — the server is started on that
# fixed address above.  Deriving from COPILOT_CLI_BASE_URL was
# misleading: if that variable pointed to a different host/port the
# exported URL would be wrong while the health check (which always
# hits localhost:8765) still passed.  Hard-code the actual address.
echo "CODEX_CLI_API_URL=http://localhost:8765" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
# Retry health-check up to 5 s to accommodate slower startup
SERVER_READY=0
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  sleep 1
  if curl -sf http://localhost:8765/api/health > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    SERVER_READY=1
    break
  fi
done
if [ "$SERVER_READY" = "1" ]; then
  echo "✅ CLI API Server ready on :8765 (PID=${CLI_API_PID})"
  echo "   BrainClient URL: http://localhost:8765"
  echo "   Import: from codex.agents.brain_client import BrainClient"
  # Report which auth token the server can use for GitHub API calls
  if [ -n "${CODEX_MASTER_KEY:-}" ]; then
    echo "   🔑 Auth: CODEX_MASTER_KEY active (full PAT — variables/secrets API ✅)"
  elif [ -n "${CODEX_BACKUP_KEY:-}" ]; then
    echo "   🔑 Auth: CODEX_BACKUP_KEY active (fallback PAT)"
  elif [ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "   🔑 Auth: GITHUB_TOKEN active (actions:write scope)"
  else
    echo "   ⚠️  No auth token — GitHub API calls will be unauthenticated (rate-limited)"
  fi
else
  echo "⚠️ CLI API Server did not respond after 5 s — see RUNNER_TEMP/cli_api_server.log"
  cat "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cli_api_server.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || true
fi
run_commands.name: 💻 Start CLI API Server (background)

EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e
echo "exit_code=$EXIT_CODE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
# Extract coverage percentage
COVERAGE_PCT=$(awk '/^TOTAL[[:space:]]/ { for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?%$/) cov = $i } END { gsub(/%/, "", cov); print cov }' "$RUNNER_TEMP/coverage_output.txt")
if ! [[ "$COVERAGE_PCT" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
  COVERAGE_PCT="unknown"
fi
if [[ "$COVERAGE_PCT" == "unknown" ]]; then
  THRESHOLD_BREACHED="true"
  echo "::warning::Coverage percentage is unknown; treating as ratchet breach."
else
  THRESHOLD_BREACHED="false"
  if ! THRESHOLD_BREACHED=$(python -c 'import sys; print(str(float(sys.argv[1]) < float(sys.argv[2])).lower())' "$COVERAGE_PCT" "$THRESHOLD"); then
    THRESHOLD_BREACHED="true"
    echo "::warning::Failed to compare coverage ($COVERAGE_PCT) against threshold ($THRESHOLD); treating as ratchet breach."
  fi
fi
echo "coverage_pct=$COVERAGE_PCT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "threshold_breached=$THRESHOLD_BREACHED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
exit $EXIT_CODE

  echo "❌ Exit codes differ - non-deterministic behavior"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "❌ **Non-deterministic behavior** - Exit codes differ (pass1: $EXIT1, pass2: $EXIT2)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  exit 1
fi

# Handle exit code 5 (no tests collected) as success
if [ "$EXIT1" = "5" ] && [ "$EXIT2" = "5" ]; then
  echo "⚠️  No determinism tests found (exit code 5) - skipping validation"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "⚠️  **No determinism tests found** - Tests are not yet implemented" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "To implement determinism tests:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "- Add @pytest.mark.determinism to tests in tests/templates/test_ml_template.py" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "- Remove @pytest.mark.skip decorators when tests are ready" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  exit 0
fi

# Handle exit code 2 (collection errors) when no tests with marker exist
# Exit code 2 typically means internal error or collection failures
# Check if the logs indicate "no tests collected" despite collection errors
if [ "$EXIT1" = "2" ] && [ "$EXIT2" = "2" ]; then
  # Check if both logs show "0 selected" (no tests matched the marker)
  SELECTED1=$(grep -E "0 selected" determinism_pass1.log || echo "")
  SELECTED2=$(grep -E "0 selected" determinism_pass2.log || echo "")

  # If both runs had collection errors but 0 tests selected, treat as "no tests"
  if [ -n "$SELECTED1" ] && [ -n "$SELECTED2" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Collection errors but no determinism tests selected (exit code 2)"
    echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "⚠️  **No determinism tests found** - Collection errors present but no tests selected" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "Details:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- pytest returned exit code 2 (collection errors) instead of 5 (no tests collected)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- This occurs when other test files have import errors during collection" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- No tests with @pytest.mark.determinism were found or executed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- Both test runs had identical results, so behavior is deterministic" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "To implement determinism tests:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- Add @pytest.mark.determinism to relevant test functions" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    exit 0
  fi

  # Otherwise, treat exit code 2 as a failure
  echo "❌ Collection errors during test execution (exit code 2)"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "❌ **Collection errors detected** - Both runs failed with exit code 2" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "Exit code 2 indicates pytest internal errors or collection failures" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  exit 1
fi

# If both runs failed with a non-zero exit code (excluding 2 and 5), treat as error
if [ "$EXIT1" != "0" ]; then
  echo "❌ Both test runs failed with exit code $EXIT1"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "❌ **Test failures detected** - Both runs failed with exit code $EXIT1" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  exit 1
fi

# Compare log outputs
if diff -u determinism_pass1.log determinism_pass2.log > determinism_diff.log; then
  echo "✅ Deterministic behavior confirmed - results identical"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "✅ **Determinism verified** - Test results are identical across runs" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
else
  echo "⚠️  Non-deterministic behavior detected - results differ"
  echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo "⚠️  **Warning**: Non-deterministic behavior detected" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo '```diff' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  head -50 determinism_diff.log >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
  exit 1
fi
run_commands.name: Compare results

if [ -s "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr_comments.jsonl" ]; then
  # Compute SINCE_DATE as the HEAD commit's authored timestamp so that only
  # @copilot comments posted AFTER the most-recent push are re-scanned.
  # This prevents an old "future session" handoff note in a previous commit's
  # comment from permanently blocking every subsequent push on a long-lived PR.
  # Fall back to 8 hours ago if git log is unavailable (shallow clone edge-case).
  HEAD_COMMIT_TIME=$(git log -1 --format="%aI" HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "${HEAD_COMMIT_TIME}" ]; then
    SINCE_DATE="${HEAD_COMMIT_TIME}"
  else
    SINCE_DATE=$(date -u -d "8 hours ago" +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" 2>/dev/null || \
                 date -u -v-8H +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" 2>/dev/null || \
                 echo "2000-01-01T00:00:00Z")
  fi
  echo "Scanning comments created after: ${SINCE_DATE}"
  python scripts/ci/check_deferral_language.py \
    --pr-comments "${RUNNER_TEMP}/pr_comments.jsonl" \
    --since "${SINCE_DATE}"
else
  echo "No agent comments to scan."
fi

# Switch the working tree to the chain-resolved target BEFORE cherry-picking
# so the commit lands on the correct staging branch, not on main.
# The initial checkout used fetch-depth=0 so HEAD_SHA is already present.
git fetch origin "${TARGET_BRANCH}" --depth=1
git checkout -B _dep_absorb_ origin/"${TARGET_BRANCH}"
# Ensure the source commit is reachable after the branch switch.
git fetch origin "${HEAD_SHA}" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "Cherry-picking ${HEAD_SHA} (${CHANGED_FILE}) from PR #${PR_NUMBER} into ${TARGET_BRANCH}…"

if [ "${DRY_RUN}" = "true" ]; then
  echo "🔍 DRY RUN — would cherry-pick ${HEAD_SHA}"
  git cherry-pick --no-commit "${HEAD_SHA}" || true
  echo "Diff preview:"
  git diff --cached --stat || true
  git cherry-pick --abort 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "✅ Dry run complete — no commit made."
  exit 0
fi

# Attempt cherry-pick; abort cleanly on conflict.
if git cherry-pick "${HEAD_SHA}"; then
  echo "✅ Cherry-pick succeeded: ${CHANGED_FILE}"
  # Push the cherry-picked commit back to the target branch.
  git push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/${TARGET_BRANCH}"
else
  echo "⚠️  Cherry-pick conflict — aborting auto-absorb for PR #${PR_NUMBER}"
  git cherry-pick --abort
  exit 0  # Non-fatal: let the human merge manually.
fi

run_commands.command:
set +e  # collect all failures before exiting

FAILED=0
CHECKED=0
FAILURES=""

# Find every requirements*.txt file under .github/
while IFS= read -r req_file; do
  CHECKED=$((CHECKED + 1))
  echo "Checking: $req_file"

  # Use pip's --dry-run (no install) to parse requirements syntax.
  # We redirect stderr to capture parse errors.
  ERR=$(python -m pip install \
    --dry-run \
    --ignore-installed \
    --no-deps \
    --no-index \
    -r "$req_file" 2>&1) || true

  # A parse error will contain "Invalid requirement" or
  # "Expected package name" — check for those specifically.
  # Note: "--no-index" always emits "Could not find a version …" for
  # every package (there is no local index), so that string must NOT
  # be treated as a failure indicator here.
  if echo "$ERR" | grep -qiE "invalid requirement|expected package name"; then
    echo "  ❌ FAILED: $req_file"
    echo "$ERR" | grep -iE "invalid requirement|expected package name" | head -5
    FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
    FAILURES="$FAILURES\n  - $req_file"
  else
    echo "  ✅ OK: $req_file"
  fi
done < <(find .github -name "requirements*.txt" | sort)

echo ""
echo "Summary: checked $CHECKED file(s), $FAILED failed."

if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "❌ The following requirements files contain invalid pip specifiers:"
  echo -e "$FAILURES"
  echo ""
  echo "Common causes:"
  echo "  • Triple-quoted Python docstrings (\"\"\"...\"\"\") at the top of the file"
  echo "  • Fix: replace docstrings with # comment lines"
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ All $CHECKED requirements file(s) under .github/ are pip-parseable."

RESOLVED_TOKEN=""
# Try GitHub App installation token first (broadest scope)
if [[ -n "${GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY}" && -n "${GITHUB_APP_ID}" && -n "${GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID}" ]]; then
  echo "ℹ️ Attempting GitHub App installation token mint..."
  INSTALL_TOKEN=$(python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import os, time, json, sys
try:
    import jwt
    key = os.environ["GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY"]
    app_id = os.environ["GITHUB_APP_ID"]
    inst_id = os.environ["GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID"]
    now = int(time.time())
    payload = {"iat": now - 60, "exp": now + 540, "iss": str(app_id)}
    app_jwt = jwt.encode(payload, key, algorithm="RS256")
    import urllib.request, urllib.error
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"https://api.github.com/app/installations/{inst_id}/access_tokens",
        method="POST",
        data=json.dumps({}).encode(),
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {app_jwt}",
            "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
            "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
            "User-Agent": "codex-discussion-cleanup/1.0",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:
            data = json.loads(resp.read())
        print(data["token"])
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as http_err:
        body = http_err.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        print(f"APP_TOKEN_FAILED: HTTP {http_err.code} {http_err.reason} — {body}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"APP_TOKEN_FAILED: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    print("")
PYEOF
)
  if [[ -n "${INSTALL_TOKEN}" && "${INSTALL_TOKEN}" != "APP_TOKEN_FAILED"* ]]; then
    RESOLVED_TOKEN="${INSTALL_TOKEN}"
    echo "✅ GitHub App installation token acquired"
    echo "auth_source=github_app" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  else
    echo "⚠️ App token mint failed — falling back to PAT"
  fi
fi
# Fallback to PAT
if [[ -z "${RESOLVED_TOKEN}" ]]; then
  if [[ -n "${CODEX_MASTER_KEY}" ]]; then

import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
from codex.skills.aais import AAISScorer

scorer = AAISScorer()
threshold = float('${AAIS_THRESHOLD}')
results = []
stale = []

for doc_dir in ['docs/agent', 'docs/admin', 'docs/how-to']:
    doc_path = Path(doc_dir)
    if not doc_path.exists():
        continue
    for md in sorted(doc_path.glob('**/*.md')):
        text = md.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
        if len(text.strip()) < 50:
            continue
        score = scorer.score(text)
        entry = {
            'file': str(md),
            'aais_total': round(score.total, 4),
            'concision': round(score.concision, 4),
            'acronym': round(score.acronym_discipline, 4),
            'structure': round(score.structure, 4),
            'clarity': round(score.clarity, 4),
            'citation': round(score.citation_lineage, 4),
        }
        results.append(entry)
        if score.total < threshold:
            stale.append(entry)

report = {
    'threshold': threshold,
    'total_docs': len(results),
    'passing': len(results) - len(stale),
    'below_threshold': len(stale),
    'stale_docs': stale,
    'all_scores': sorted(results, key=lambda x: x['aais_total']),
}

Path('.codex').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
Path('.codex/doc_refresh_report.json').write_text(
    json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8'
)

print(f'📊 Scanned {len(results)} docs | Threshold: {threshold}')
print(f'✅ Passing: {len(results) - len(stale)}')
print(f'⚠️  Below threshold: {len(stale)}')
if stale:
    print()
    print('Files below AAIS threshold:')
    for s in stale:
        print(f'  {s[\"aais_total\"]:.3f}  {s[\"file\"]}')

# Non-blocking: always exit 0
sys.exit(0)
"

run_commands.command:
EVENT="${{ github.event_name }}"

# Shared exclusion filter applied to every scan mode
_find_all_md() {
  find . -name "*.md" \
    -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
    -not -path "./.git/*" \
    -not -path "./temp/*" \
    -not -path "./archive/*" \
    -not -path "./cognitive_app/node_modules/*" \
    -not -path "./.github/workflows/*" \
    | sort
}

if [ "$EVENT" = "schedule" ]; then
  echo "📅 Scheduled run — full scan (excluding .github/workflows/)"
  FILES=$(_find_all_md)
else
  # Diff-based: only files changed vs the merge base
  BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.before || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
  if [ -z "$BASE_SHA" ] || [ "$BASE_SHA" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
    BASE_SHA="HEAD~1"
  fi
  # Build the changed list; fall back to full scan if diff fails (e.g. shallow)
  DIFF_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA" HEAD -- '*.md' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -v '^\.github/workflows/' \
    | grep -v '^node_modules/' \
    | grep -v '^temp/' \
    | grep -v '^archive/' \
    | xargs -I{} sh -c '[ -f "{}" ] && echo "{}"' 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ -z "$DIFF_FILES" ] && [ "$BASE_SHA" != "HEAD~1" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Diff empty or failed — falling back to full scan"
    FILES=$(_find_all_md)
  else
    FILES="$DIFF_FILES"
  fi
  echo "📝 Diff-based: $(echo "$FILES" | grep -c . || echo 0) file(s) to check"
fi

echo "$FILES" > /tmp/md_files.txt

echo "file_count=$FILE_COUNT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "📊 Candidate file count: $FILE_COUNT"

import json, hashlib, os

CACHE_FILE = ".link-check-per-file.json"
MD_FILES_LIST = "/tmp/md_files.txt"

# Load previous per-file results
prev = {}
if os.path.exists(CACHE_FILE):
    try:
        with open(CACHE_FILE) as f:
            prev = json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        prev = {}

# Read candidate files
with open(MD_FILES_LIST) as f:
    files = [ln.strip() for ln in f if ln.strip()]

to_check = []
for fp in files:
    if not os.path.isfile(fp):
        continue
    with open(fp, "rb") as _fh:
        _sha = hashlib.sha1()
        while chunk := _fh.read(65536):
            _sha.update(chunk)
        h = _sha.hexdigest()
    if prev.get(fp) != h:
        to_check.append(fp)

with open("/tmp/md_changed.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(to_check))

print(f"Candidate files: {len(files)}, Changed/new: {len(to_check)}")
with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a") as fh:
    fh.write(f"changed_count={len(to_check)}\n")
PYEOF

    with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a") as f:

    with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a") as f:

now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

status = "fresh"

    print(f"::error::RAG index is {age_hours:.1f}h old (>{STALE_ERROR_HOURS}h) — stale rebuild required")
    status = "stale_error"

    echo "🔀 Push target: ${TARGET_REF} (reason: ${{ steps.resolve-target.outputs.reason }})"
  else
    TARGET_REF="${{ github.ref_name }}"
  fi
  echo "🔄 Re-basing HAR commit onto tip of ${TARGET_REF} before push"
  git fetch origin "${TARGET_REF}"
  git rebase "origin/${TARGET_REF}"
  git push origin HEAD:${TARGET_REF}
  echo "✅ HAR committed and pushed (LFS)"
fi

run_commands.name: Write job summary

remediation_notes: Found 1 explicit root file references that will break on cleanup

run_commands.command:
set -euo pipefail

# If explicit list provided, use it directly
if [[ -n "${ISSUE_OVERRIDE:-}" ]]; then
  echo "issues=${ISSUE_OVERRIDE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "source=manual-override" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "ℹ️  Using manual issue override: ${ISSUE_OVERRIDE}"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ -z "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]]; then
  echo "issues=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "source=none" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "ℹ️  No PR number — skipping issue extraction"
  exit 0
fi

# Fetch PR body and extract issue references
# Use || true so a transient API rate-limit or network error does not
# fail the gate — in that case we simply find no issue references and
# exit 0 (non-blocking).
PR_BODY=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}" \
  --jq '.body // ""' 2>/dev/null) || {
  echo "⚠️  Could not fetch PR body (API error / rate limit) — skipping issue extraction"
  echo "issues=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "source=api-error" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  exit 0
}

# Only extract issues explicitly targeted for closure (matches GitHub
# auto-close semantics).  Bare "#N" references are informational and
# should NOT trigger the resolution gate — they are cross-references,
# not closure directives.
RAW_NUMBERS=$(echo "${PR_BODY}" | \
  grep -oP '(?i)(?:close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\s+#\K\d+' | \
  sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | xargs || true)

# Exclude the current PR number to avoid circular dependency:
# the gate checking its own PR → BLOCKED (because this gate is
# failing) → exit 1 → gate stays failed forever.
ISSUE_NUMBERS=""
for n in ${RAW_NUMBERS}; do
  if [[ "$n" != "${PR_NUMBER}" ]]; then
    ISSUE_NUMBERS="${ISSUE_NUMBERS} ${n}"
  else
    echo "ℹ️  Excluding self-reference #${n} (this PR)"
  fi
done
ISSUE_NUMBERS=$(echo "${ISSUE_NUMBERS}" | xargs || true)

echo "issues=${ISSUE_NUMBERS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "source=pr-body" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "${ISSUE_NUMBERS}" ]]; then
  echo "ℹ️  Found issue references in PR #${PR_NUMBER}: ${ISSUE_NUMBERS}"
else
  echo "ℹ️  No issue references found in PR body"
fi
run_commands.name: Extract issue references from PR body

run_commands.command:
# Guard: never heal failures from auto-fix workflows themselves.
# This prevents recursive healer↔autofix feedback loops.
case "${TRIGGERING_WORKFLOW}" in
  "Auto-Fix Common CI Issues"|"PR Auto-Fix Check")
    echo "::notice::Healer skipped — triggering workflow is ${TRIGGERING_WORKFLOW} (recursive loop guard)"
    echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

# Guard: skip if the triggering commit message contains [skip ci].
# Cascade vector: sweep pushes [skip ci] commit → some workflow_run still
# fires (e.g. workflow_run triggered by the completed healer itself on a
# different branch) → healer would re-run unnecessarily.
# Use nested if/elif to avoid grep executing when the feature is disabled.
if [[ "${CODEX_HEALER_SKIP_SKIPCI}" == "true" ]]; then
  # ${TRIGGERING_COMMIT_MSG:0:80} — bash substring (supported by bash 4+,
  # which is the GitHub Actions default shell). Used for truncated logging only.
  COMMIT_PREVIEW="${TRIGGERING_COMMIT_MSG:0:80}"
  if echo "${TRIGGERING_COMMIT_MSG}" | grep -qi '\[skip ci\]'; then
    echo "::notice::Healer skipped — triggering commit contains [skip ci]: '${COMMIT_PREVIEW}'"
    echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### ⏭️ Healer Skipped — [skip ci] Commit" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Triggering commit contains \`[skip ci]\` — skipping healer to break sweep→validate→healer cascade." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Hard brake: if >= N Iterative Self-Healing CI runs have been triggered
# for this branch in the past hour, skip this run. This prevents the
# self-healing cascade (issue #3860) where healer failures re-trigger the
# healer indefinitely (SELF_HEALING_001 sub-scenario C).
# Default 5 (lowered from 10→5 in S177). Override via CODEX_MAX_HEALER_RUNS_PER_HOUR.
MAX_PER_HOUR="${CODEX_MAX_HEALER_RUNS_PER_HOUR:-5}"
ONE_HOUR_AGO=$(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null \
  || date -u -v-1H +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "")
if [ -n "$ONE_HOUR_AGO" ] && [ -n "$HEAD_BRANCH" ]; then
  RECENT=$(gh api \
    "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/iterative-self-healing-ci.yml/runs?branch=${HEAD_BRANCH}&per_page=50&created=>=${ONE_HOUR_AGO}" \
    --jq '.total_count' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [ "$RECENT" -ge "$MAX_PER_HOUR" ]; then
    echo "::warning::Self-healing run cap reached: ${RECENT} runs in the last hour on ${HEAD_BRANCH} (max ${MAX_PER_HOUR}). Skipping to break cascade (issue #3860 SELF_HEALING_001)."
    echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### 🛑 Cascade Brake Activated" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Run cap: **${RECENT}** healer runs in the past hour on \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\` (max ${MAX_PER_HOUR})." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Skipping this run to break self-healing cascade (SELF_HEALING_001)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "See: [issue #3860](https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/3860)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    exit 0
  fi
fi
echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
run_commands.name: Per-branch hourly run-cap guard (cascade brake)

run_commands.command:
# Resilient pip install: prefer venv binary but recreate the venv on cache miss
# so the triage job never fails due to a missing venv and never pollutes the
# system/user site-packages with an un-isolated install.
# Root cause of 126 self-healing failures (CI health alert 2026-03-21):
# the venv pip launcher was unavailable on cache misses, causing triage to exit 1
# before classify-run could run, which marked the whole workflow as failed.
# S177 hardening (issue #3977): rm stale venv + --clear + pip upgrade to
# prevent corrupted partial-cache-restore venvs from causing silent failures.
PYTHON_BIN="${VENV_PYTHON:-.venv_ci/bin/python}"
if ! "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install requests --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
  rm -rf .venv_ci
  python3 -m venv --clear .venv_ci
  PYTHON_BIN=".venv_ci/bin/python"
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools --quiet
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install requests --quiet
fi
echo "run_id=${TRIGGERING_RUN_ID}"       >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "head_sha=${HEAD_SHA}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "head_branch=${HEAD_BRANCH}"         >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "workflow_name=${TRIGGERING_RUN_NAME}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
# Extract PR number from workflow_run event; fall back to empty string
PR_NUM=$(echo "${GITHUB_EVENT_PATH:+$(python3 -c "import json,os; d=json.load(open(os.environ['GITHUB_EVENT_PATH'])); print(d.get('workflow_run',{}).get('pull_requests',[{}])[0].get('number','') if d.get('workflow_run',{}).get('pull_requests') else '')" 2>/dev/null)}" || echo "")
echo "pr_number=${PR_NUM}"                >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# D-00: Use collect_telemetry --classify-run to categorise the failure.
# The --classify-run flag (added S150) fetches run+jobs via the GitHub API
# and returns one of 15 pattern names (ruff-*, import-*, yaml-*, etc.).
PATTERN=$(python3 scripts/ci/collect_telemetry.py \
  --classify-run "$TRIGGERING_RUN_ID" \
  --owner Aries-Serpent --repo _codex_ \
  --token "$GH_TOKEN" 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")

echo "pattern=${PATTERN}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Expanded fixable patterns (Phase 5 — S154 + S163):
# Added changelog-* (check_7 CHANGELOG cross-PR), pip-cache-* (sparse checkout),
# policy-gate-* (pre-create pip cache fix), rebase-gate-* (branch gate),
# auth-delegation (REQ-10 branch-diverged caused by scheduled bot commits).
# push-race: sweep/heal push race — auto_fix is a no-op but baseline-sweep handles it.
# integration-branch-direct-session: NOT fixable — structural redirect only.
# self-healing: NOT fixable — cascade detection; see SELF_HEALING_001 pattern.
case "$PATTERN" in
  ruff-*|import-*|yaml-*|timeout-config|unused-import|auto-fix|\
  changelog-*|pip-cache-*|policy-gate-*|rebase-gate-*|mypy-baseline|\
  auth-delegation|branch-diverged|push-race|autostash-race)
    echo "fixable=true"  >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    ;;
  self-healing)
    # Self-healing cascade detected (SELF_HEALING_001):
    # The triggering workflow is itself an Iterative Self-Healing CI run.
    # Most common root cause: the venv pip launcher being unavailable on cache miss caused
    # triage to fail before classify-run could run (fixed in S172).
    # This pattern is not auto-fixable here — it indicates the self-healing
    # loop itself has an infrastructure issue.  Emit a clear summary for
    # the ci-health-alert-agent to detect and report.
    echo "fixable=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### ⚠️ Self-Healing Cascade Detected (SELF_HEALING_001)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "The failing workflow **is** an Iterative Self-Healing CI run." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "This is a cascade failure: the healer itself is failing." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Probable cause:** the cached venv pip launcher was unavailable on cache miss." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Fix applied in S172:** on cache miss the venv is recreated with \`python3 -m venv .venv_ci\` (both triage and heal jobs)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**If this persists:** Check \`.github/actions/setup-python-cached/action.yml\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "and verify \`.venv_ci/\` is created even on full cache miss." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "See: [\`SELF_HEALING_001\`](.codex/patterns/ci_failure_patterns.yaml)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ;;
  integration-branch-direct-session)
    # REQ-11: session on integration branch — non-fixable; needs sub-PR creation.
    # Post an informative escalation comment and skip auto-fix.
    echo "fixable=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### 🚫 REQ-11: Integration-Branch Direct-Session Detected" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Pattern \`integration-branch-direct-session\` is **not auto-fixable**." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "The PR head is the staging integration branch (\`0D_base_\`)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Fix:** Create a sub-PR targeting \`0D_base_\` instead:" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "\`\`\`bash" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "gh workflow run copilot-session-chain.yml -f source_branch=0D_base_ -f session_title=\"<task>\"" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "\`\`\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "See: [INTEGRATION_BRANCH_MODEL.md](.codex/docs/INTEGRATION_BRANCH_MODEL.md)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ;;
  coverage-timeout)
    # Coverage/test timeout failure (P19 pattern): pre-existing shadow-import
    # failures (config.openai_client, services.github.client) cause the
    # Resilient Validation Suite and Pre-Merge Validation to time out.
    # Not auto-fixable here — root cause is upstream module shadow imports.
    # Escalated to Copilot Coding Agent via copilot-escalation job.
    echo "fixable=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### ⏱️ Coverage / Test Timeout (P19)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Pattern \`coverage-timeout\` is **not auto-fixable** at this layer." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Root cause:** Pre-existing P19 shadow-import failures in" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "\`config.openai_client\` / \`services.github.client\` cause test-suite" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "timeouts in the Resilient Validation Suite and Pre-Merge Validation." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Affected test files:**" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "- \`tests/config/test_openai_client.py\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "- \`tests/services/github/test_client.py\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "- \`tests/services/test_github_client_phase9_1.py\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Action:** These failures pre-date this PR. Copilot escalation will" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "be triggered to investigate and fix the shadow-import root cause." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ;;
  unknown)
    # Pattern unrecognised by collect_telemetry.py classify-run.
    # This occurs when: (a) the run log is not yet available, (b) no
    # known keyword matches, or (c) classify-run itself failed.
    # Not auto-fixable — escalate to human + Copilot for investigation.
    echo "fixable=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "### ❓ Unknown Failure Pattern" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "Pattern \`unknown\` — \`collect_telemetry.py --classify-run\` could not" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "identify the failure from the run logs." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Common causes:**" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "1. Run logs not yet available (retry in a few minutes)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "2. New failure type not in the pattern keyword dictionary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "3. \`classify-run\` itself threw an exception (check triage logs)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "**Action:** To add this pattern, update \`PATTERN_KEYWORDS\` in" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "\`scripts/ci/collect_telemetry.py\` and add a \`case\` arm in this workflow." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "See: [\`docs/workflows/WORKFLOW_RACE_CONDITION_AUDIT.md\`](docs/workflows/WORKFLOW_RACE_CONDITION_AUDIT.md)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "fixable=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    ;;
esac

echo "### 🩺 D-00 Failure Triage"                              >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Key | Value |"                                          >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "|-----|-------|"                                          >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Run | [\`${TRIGGERING_RUN_ID}\`](https://github.com/Aries-Serpent/_codex_/actions/runs/${TRIGGERING_RUN_ID}) |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Workflow | ${TRIGGERING_RUN_NAME} |"                   >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Pattern | \`${PATTERN}\` |"                            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Branch | \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\` |"                         >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "| Agent Auth Enabled | \`${AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED}\` |"      >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
FIXABLE=$(grep '^fixable=' "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)
echo "| Auto-fixable | \`${FIXABLE}\` |"                       >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
run_commands.name: Classify failure (D-00 — collect_telemetry --classify-run)

_0D_EXISTS=false
if gh api "repos/${REPO}/branches/0D_base_" --silent 2>/dev/null; then

fi

git fetch origin main --depth=5 --no-tags 2>/dev/null || true
git restore --source=origin/main -- \
  .github/actions/setup-python-cached/action.yml \

# Resilient pip install: prefer venv binary but recreate the venv on cache miss
# instead of installing to system/user site-packages (same fix as triage — S172).
# S177 hardening (issue #3977): rm stale venv + --clear + pip upgrade.
PYTHON_BIN="${VENV_PYTHON:-.venv_ci/bin/python}"
if ! "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install ruff black isort --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
  rm -rf .venv_ci

  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install ruff black isort --quiet

bash scripts/ci/ci_triage_repro.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/pre_triage.txt
EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "pre_triage_exit=${EXIT_CODE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "### D-07 Pre-Heal Triage" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

run_commands.name: D-07 — Run ci_triage_repro.sh (pre-heal baseline)

run_commands.command:
echo "Applying auto-fix for pattern: ${PATTERN} (iteration ${ITERATION})"

# ── Branch-diverged / auth-delegation: call branch_rebase_check.py ──
# These patterns fire when a PR branch is behind/diverged from its base
# because scheduled bot workflows commit directly to main every 2-24 h.
# branch_rebase_check.py --auto-merge-skip-ci resolves this via the
# GitHub Merges API without any git checkout, then posts the rich helper
# comment with conflict analysis + Copilot agent prompt to the PR and
# updates the PR Status Dashboard section.
if [[ "$PATTERN" == "auth-delegation" || "$PATTERN" == "branch-diverged" || "$PATTERN" == "rebase-gate"* ]]; then
  PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list --head "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
    --repo Aries-Serpent/_codex_ --json number -q '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
    echo "  Running branch_rebase_check.py --auto-merge-skip-ci for PR #${PR_NUMBER}…"
    python scripts/ci/branch_rebase_check.py \
      --repo Aries-Serpent/_codex_ \
      --pr "${PR_NUMBER}" \
      --auto-merge-skip-ci \
      --post-comment \
      --upsert-dashboard \
      --github-output \
      --github-summary \
      2>&1 | tee /tmp/fix_output.txt
    # The script merges via API — no local file changes to stage
    echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "✅ Branch rebase check/auto-merge complete" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  else
    echo "  ⚠️ Could not determine PR number for branch ${HEAD_BRANCH}"
    echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  fi
else
  # ── All other patterns: run auto_fix_common_issues.py with --pattern ──
  # The --pattern-name flag correctly runs only the matching pattern,
  # making each iteration faster and the diff more targeted.
  python scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py --pattern-name "${PATTERN}" \
    2>&1 | tee /tmp/fix_output.txt
  if [ "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" -ne 0 ]; then
    # --pattern-name found no match; fall back to running all patterns
    python scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py \
      2>&1 | tee /tmp/fix_output.txt
  fi
fi

# Restore overlaid trusted scripts — only actual fix outputs should be staged
if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/overlaid_scripts.txt" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  git restore -- $(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/overlaid_scripts.txt") 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if git diff --quiet; then
  echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "⚠️ No file changes produced for pattern \`${PATTERN}\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
else
  echo "changed=true"  >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only | tr '\n' ',')
  echo "changed_files=${CHANGED_FILES}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "✅ Changes produced: ${CHANGED_FILES}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi
run_commands.name: Apply auto-fix

run_commands.command:
# Full YAML compliance check
python3 - << 'PYEOF'
import os, yaml, sys
wf = ".github/workflows"
errors = []
for root, _, files in os.walk(wf):
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith((".yml", ".yaml")):
            path = os.path.join(root, f)
            try:
                yaml.safe_load(open(path))
            except yaml.YAMLError as e:
                errors.append(f"{path}: {e}")
if errors:
    for e in errors:
        print(f"❌ {e}")
    sys.exit(1)
print(f"✅ All workflow files parse cleanly")
PYEOF
# Ruff check
ruff check src/ --quiet 2>&1 | tee /tmp/ruff_output.txt
# Run ci_triage_repro.sh for full 7-check validation
bash scripts/ci/ci_triage_repro.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/post_triage.txt
TRIAGE_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "triage_exit=${TRIAGE_EXIT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [ "${TRIAGE_EXIT}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "valid=true"  >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "valid=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
echo "### D-07 Post-Heal Triage" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
cat /tmp/post_triage.txt | grep -E "✅|❌|PASS|FAIL|Summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
run_commands.name: D-07 — Validate fix (ci_triage_repro.sh post-heal)

run_commands.command:
# Write attempt record to .codex/healing_attempts/ so future sessions
# can review what was tried, what worked, and what failed.
# Use Python json.dumps() to guarantee valid JSON regardless of special
# characters (quotes, backslashes, etc.) in captured log text.
ATTEMPT_DIR=".codex/healing_attempts"
mkdir -p "${ATTEMPT_DIR}"
export TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
export ATTEMPT_FILE="${ATTEMPT_DIR}/${TIMESTAMP//[:T]/-}_${PATTERN}_iter${ITERATION}.json"
export PRE_TRIAGE=$(cat /tmp/pre_triage.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Summary|✅|❌' | head -5 | tr '\n' '|' || true)
export POST_TRIAGE=$(cat /tmp/post_triage.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Summary|✅|❌' | head -5 | tr '\n' '|' || true)
export FIX_OUTPUT=$(cat /tmp/fix_output.txt 2>/dev/null | head -10 | tr '\n' '|' || true)
python3 - << 'PYEOF'
import json, os, sys
data = {
    "timestamp":   os.environ["TIMESTAMP"],
    "run_id":      os.environ["RUN_ID"],
    "head_branch": os.environ["HEAD_BRANCH"],
    "pattern":     os.environ["PATTERN"],
    "iteration":   int(os.environ.get("ITERATION", 0) or 0),
    "changed":     os.environ.get("CHANGED", "false").lower() == "true",
    "valid":       os.environ.get("VALID", "false").lower() == "true",
    "workflow":    "iterative-self-healing-ci",
    "pre_triage":  os.environ.get("PRE_TRIAGE", ""),
    "post_triage": os.environ.get("POST_TRIAGE", ""),
    "fix_output":  os.environ.get("FIX_OUTPUT", ""),
}
with open(os.environ["ATTEMPT_FILE"], "w") as fh:
    json.dump(data, fh, indent=2)
print(f"Attempt record: {os.environ['ATTEMPT_FILE']}")
PYEOF
run_commands.name: Record attempt (success or failure)

run_commands.command:
# Forward each heal attempt to the PDA Loop failure logger so that
# grounded solutions accumulate across sessions and can be queried by
# future agents (python scripts/ci/pda_failure_logger.py summarize).
if [ ! -f scripts/ci/pda_failure_logger.py ]; then
  echo "::notice::pda_failure_logger.py not found — skipping PDA log"
  exit 0
fi
SESSION_ID="S${SESSION:-auto}-heal"
if [ "${CHANGED}" = "true" ]; then
  # A fix was applied — log it
  PASSED_FLAG=""
  [ "${VALID}" = "true" ] && PASSED_FLAG="--verification-passed"
  FIX_SUMMARY=$(cat /tmp/fix_output.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -E '✅|fixed|patched' | head -3 | tr '\n' '; ' || echo "auto-fix applied")
  python3 scripts/ci/pda_failure_logger.py log-fix \
    --session "${SESSION_ID}" \
    --pr "${PR_NUMBER:-0}" \
    --branch "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
    --pattern-id "RP-AUTO-$(echo "$PATTERN" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')" \
    --fix-applied "${FIX_SUMMARY}" \
    --verification-cmd "bash scripts/ci/ci_triage_repro.sh" \
    ${PASSED_FLAG} 2>/dev/null || true
else
  # No fix was applied — log the failure for grounding
  ERR_TEXT=$(cat /tmp/pre_triage.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -E '❌|ERROR|FAIL' | head -3 | tr '\n' '; ' || echo "")
  python3 scripts/ci/pda_failure_logger.py log-failure \
    --session "${SESSION_ID}" \
    --pr "${PR_NUMBER:-0}" \
    --branch "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
    --pattern-id "RP-AUTO-$(echo "$PATTERN" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')" \
    --workflow "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" \
    --workflow-run "${RUN_ID}" \
    --error-text "${ERR_TEXT:0:400}" \
    --root-cause "Pattern ${PATTERN} not auto-fixable at iteration ${ITERATION}" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
UPPER_PATTERN=$(echo "$PATTERN" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
echo "### 📊 PDA pattern logged: RP-AUTO-${UPPER_PATTERN}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
run_commands.name: Log pattern to PDA Loop + AfterMath

run_commands.command:
if [ "${AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED}" != "true" ]; then
  echo "⚠️ COPILOT_AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED is not 'true' — autonomous push may fail."
  echo "   Set COPILOT_AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED=true via Agent Token Delegation workflow."
fi
# For PR branches push fixes back to the same branch.
# For main / empty head_branch walk the staging chain instead.
if [ -n "${HEAD_BRANCH}" ] && [ "${HEAD_BRANCH}" != "main" ]; then
  TARGET_BRANCH="${HEAD_BRANCH}"
else
  TARGET_BRANCH="${RESOLVE_TARGET_BRANCH:-main}"
  echo "🔀 Push target resolved: ${TARGET_BRANCH} (reason: ${RESOLVE_TARGET_REASON})"
fi
git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
# Reconfigure remote with token since persist-credentials: false was used on checkout.
# This ensures git push uses the token without persisting it in the working tree
# where untrusted checked-out code could read it.
git remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
# Stage only the files explicitly changed by the fix scripts
# (plus the healing-attempts record). Avoid git add -A which would
# stage every difference between HEAD and the remote.
# We are already on the target branch (checked out in the first step),
# so no git reset is needed — the working tree is already at the correct
# branch tip and the fix-script changes are relative to that content.
IFS=',' read -ra FILES <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
for f in "${FILES[@]}"; do
  f="${f// /}"
  if [ -n "$f" ]; then
    git add -- "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
done
git add ".codex/healing_attempts/" 2>/dev/null || true
git commit -m "self-heal(iter-${MATRIX_ITERATION}): auto-fix ${PATTERN} [skip ci]

Autonomous Phase 5 self-heal — pattern: ${PATTERN}
Iteration: ${MATRIX_ITERATION} | Run: https://github.com/Aries-Serpent/_codex_/actions/runs/${TRIAGE_RUN_ID}
COPILOT_AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED: ${AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED}"
# Retry push up to 3 times with rebase to handle concurrent push race
# (SELF_HEALING_001 sub-scenario B: multiple heal jobs push simultaneously).
_pushed=false
for _attempt in 1 2 3; do
  _pull_err=$(git pull --rebase --autostash origin "${TARGET_BRANCH}" 2>&1) || \
    echo "::warning::git pull attempt ${_attempt} non-zero: ${_pull_err}"
  if _push_err=$(git push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/${TARGET_BRANCH}" 2>&1); then
    _pushed=true
    break
  else
    echo "::warning::Push attempt ${_attempt} failed — retrying in 5s: ${_push_err}"
    sleep 5
  fi
done
if [ "${_pushed}" != "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::Heal push failed after 3 attempts — concurrent push race detected"
  exit 1
fi
run_commands.name: Commit and push fix (requires COPILOT_AGENT_AUTH_ENABLED=true)

run_commands.command:
echo "### Self-Heal Iteration ${MATRIX_ITERATION}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "- Pattern: \`${TRIAGE_PATTERN}\`"      >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "- Changed: \`${FIX_CHANGED}\`"   >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "- Valid:   \`${FIX_VALID}\`"      >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "- Files:   \`${FIX_CHANGED_FILES}\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
run_commands.name: Report iteration

run_commands.command:
git fetch origin main --depth=3 --no-tags 2>/dev/null || true
git restore --source=origin/main -- \
  .github/actions/setup-python-cached/action.yml \
  scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py \
  scripts/ci/sync_tracked_files.py \
  scripts/ci/session_wrapup_autofix.py \
  2>/dev/null || true
echo "scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py scripts/ci/sync_tracked_files.py scripts/ci/session_wrapup_autofix.py" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/overlaid_sweep.txt"

run_commands.command:
PYTHON_BIN="${VENV_PYTHON:-.venv_ci/bin/python}"
if ! "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install detect-secrets --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
  rm -rf .venv_ci
  python3 -m venv --clear .venv_ci
  PYTHON_BIN=".venv_ci/bin/python"
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools --quiet
  "$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install detect-secrets ruff --quiet

run_commands.command:
echo "### 🔄 Universal Baseline Sweep" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Step 1: Sync .secrets.baseline (most common root cause — SCP-RESCUE-5)
python scripts/ci/sync_tracked_files.py --fix --manifest-only 2>&1 | tee /tmp/sweep_sync.txt
SYNC_STATUS=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
cat /tmp/sweep_sync.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Step 2: Run all auto-fixable patterns (ruff, coverage, isort, etc.)
python scripts/ci/auto_fix_common_issues.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/sweep_fix.txt
cat /tmp/sweep_fix.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Restore trusted scripts so they're not staged as branch changes
if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/overlaid_sweep.txt" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  git restore -- $(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/overlaid_sweep.txt") 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if git diff --quiet; then
  echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "✅ No changes required — baseline already clean" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
else
  echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "changed_files=${CHANGED_FILES}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "📝 Files changed by sweep: ${CHANGED_FILES}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi
run_commands.name: Run universal sweep

run_commands.command:
PROTECTED_BRANCHES=("main" "0D_base_")
_is_protected=false
for _prot in "${PROTECTED_BRANCHES[@]}"; do
  if [[ "${HEAD_BRANCH}" == "${_prot}" ]]; then
    _is_protected=true
    break
  fi
done

# Manual override guard (admin-toggled variable)
if [[ "${CODEX_SWEEP_SKIP_MAIN}" == "true" && "${_is_protected}" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "::warning::CODEX_SWEEP_SKIP_MAIN=true — skipping sweep push to protected branch '${HEAD_BRANCH}'."
  echo "### ⏭️ Sweep Push Skipped — CODEX_SWEEP_SKIP_MAIN" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo "Set repo variable \`CODEX_SWEEP_SKIP_MAIN=false\` to re-enable." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  exit 0
fi

# S933 guard: never auto-push sweep commits to active PR head branches.
# These housekeeping pushes frequently create branch divergence and merge conflicts
# during active coding sessions.
if [[ "${HEAD_BRANCH}" =~ ^copilot/ ]]; then
  echo "::warning::Skipping sweep push to active PR branch '${HEAD_BRANCH}' to prevent rebase/merge-conflict churn."
  echo "### ⏭️ Sweep Push Skipped — active PR branch guard" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo "Branch \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\` is a Copilot PR branch; sweep commit deferred." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  exit 0
fi

# S933 guard: if protected branch has any open PRs, defer sweep pushes entirely.
# Goal: keep main/0D_base_ stable while PRs are in flight to avoid cross-PR conflicts.
if [[ "${_is_protected}" == "true" ]]; then
  _open_pr_probe_count=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls?base=${HEAD_BRANCH}&state=open&per_page=1" \
    --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  _open_pr_exists=false
  if [[ "${_open_pr_probe_count}" -gt "0" ]]; then
    _open_pr_exists=true
  fi
  if [[ "${_open_pr_exists}" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "::warning::At least one open PR targets '${HEAD_BRANCH}' — skipping sweep push."
    echo "### ⏭️ Sweep Push Deferred — protected branch active-PR guard" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    echo "An open PR targets \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\`. Sweep commit deferred to avoid merge conflicts." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Automatic open-PR conflict guard — applies when pushing to main or 0D_base_.
# If any open PR targeting this branch touches the same files the sweep changes,
# defer the push to prevent merge conflicts in long-lived PRs.
if [[ "${_is_protected}" == "true" ]]; then
  SWEEP_FILES=$(git diff --name-only HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "${SWEEP_FILES}" ]; then
    OPEN_PRS=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls?base=${HEAD_BRANCH}&state=open&per_page=100" \
      --jq '.[].number' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    _conflict_pr=""
    for PR_NUM in ${OPEN_PRS}; do
      PR_FILES=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR_NUM}/files?per_page=100" \
        --jq '.[].filename' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      while IFS= read -r sweep_file; do
        if echo "${PR_FILES}" | grep -qxF "${sweep_file}"; then
          _conflict_pr="${PR_NUM}"
          break 2
        fi
      done <<< "${SWEEP_FILES}"
    done
    if [ -n "${_conflict_pr}" ]; then
      echo "::warning::Open PR #${_conflict_pr} touches the same files — deferring sweep push to '${HEAD_BRANCH}' to prevent merge conflict."
      echo "### ⏭️ Sweep Push Deferred — open-PR conflict guard" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      echo "Open PR #${_conflict_pr} touches the same files. Push to \`${HEAD_BRANCH}\` deferred." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      echo "The sweep will be applied the next time the conflicting PR merges." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      exit 0
    fi
  fi
fi

git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
# Reconfigure remote with token since persist-credentials: false was used on checkout.
git remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
git add -A
git diff --cached --stat
# [skip ci] prevents push-triggered workflows from re-triggering the healer
git commit -m "fix(ci): universal baseline sweep — sync+auto_fix [skip ci]"
# Retry push up to 3 times with rebase to handle concurrent push race on main
# (SELF_HEALING_001 sub-scenario B: multiple sweep jobs push simultaneously).
_pushed=false
for _attempt in 1 2 3; do
  _pull_err=$(git pull --rebase --autostash origin "${HEAD_BRANCH}" 2>&1) || \
    echo "::warning::git pull attempt ${_attempt} non-zero: ${_pull_err}"
  if _push_err=$(git push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/${HEAD_BRANCH}" 2>&1); then
    _pushed=true
    break
  else
    echo "::warning::Push attempt ${_attempt} failed — retrying in 5s: ${_push_err}"
    sleep 5
  fi
done
if [ "${_pushed}" != "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::Sweep push failed after 3 attempts — concurrent push race detected"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Sweep commit pushed to ${HEAD_BRANCH}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
run_commands.name: Commit and push sweep fixes

run_commands.command:
python scripts/ci/post_rescue_comment.py
echo "### Escalated to human review" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "Pattern \`${{ needs.triage.outputs.pattern }}\` is not auto-fixable." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "Appended to CI rescue thread for commit \`${{ needs.triage.outputs.head_sha }}\`." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
run_commands.name: Append escalation to canonical CI rescue thread (S298)

run_commands.command:
# Emit compact Markdown tables for (a) high-recurrence and
# (b) cross-PR correlation (Phase 8 P3).
# Falls back to empty string gracefully if DB absent or python fails.
python3 - <<'PYEOF' > /tmp/_hr_output.txt 2>/dev/null || true
import os, sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/ci")
try:
    import pattern_recorder as pr
    db = os.environ.get("CODEX_DB_PATH", os.path.expanduser("~/.codex/cli_history.db"))
    conn = pr._open_db(db)

    # --- High-recurrence table ---
    rows = pr.high_recurrence(conn, min_occurrences=3, min_fix_rate=0.0)
    if rows:
        lines = ["| Pattern | Total | Fix% |",
                 "|---------|-------|------|"]
        for r in rows[:5]:
            lines.append(f"| `{r['pattern_name']}` | {r['total']} | {r['fix_rate']*100:.0f}% |")
        hr_table = "\n".join(lines)
    else:
        hr_table = ""

    # --- Cross-PR correlation table (Phase 8 P3) ---
    cross = pr.cross_pr_correlation(conn, min_prs=2)
    if cross:
        clines = ["| Pattern | PRs | Total |",
                  "|---------|-----|-------|"]
        for r in cross[:5]:
            clines.append(f"| `{r['pattern_name']}` | {r['pr_count']} | {r['total']} |")
        cross_table = "\n".join(clines)
    else:
        cross_table = ""

    print(f"HR_TABLE={hr_table}")
    print(f"CROSS_TABLE={cross_table}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"HR_TABLE=")
    print(f"CROSS_TABLE=")
PYEOF

# Parse outputs safely
HR_TABLE=$(grep '^HR_TABLE=' /tmp/_hr_output.txt | cut -d'=' -f2- || echo "")
CROSS_TABLE=$(grep '^CROSS_TABLE=' /tmp/_hr_output.txt | cut -d'=' -f2- || echo "")
{
  echo "table<<HREOF"
  echo "$HR_TABLE"
  echo "HREOF"
  echo "cross_table<<CROSSEOF"
  echo "$CROSS_TABLE"
  echo "CROSSEOF"
} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
run_commands.name: Query high-recurrence + cross-PR patterns

run_commands.command:
# Export the pattern knowledge graph as JSON and upload as artifact.
# This gives cross-run persistence without requiring git commits.
python3 - <<'PYEOF' > /tmp/pattern_snapshot.json 2>/dev/null || echo '{}' > /tmp/pattern_snapshot.json
import os, sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/ci")
try:
    import pattern_recorder as pr
    db = os.environ.get("CODEX_DB_PATH", os.path.expanduser("~/.codex/cli_history.db"))
    conn = pr._open_db(db)
    snapshot = pr.export_json(conn)
    print(json.dumps(snapshot, indent=2))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({"error": str(e), "patterns": [], "summary": {}}))
PYEOF
echo "Pattern DB snapshot written to /tmp/pattern_snapshot.json"
wc -l /tmp/pattern_snapshot.json || true
run_commands.name: Snapshot pattern DB → workflow artifact (Phase 8 P2)

run_commands.command:
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list --head "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
  --repo Aries-Serpent/_codex_ --json number -q '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

if [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
  echo "::warning::No open PR found for branch '${HEAD_BRANCH}' — creating GitHub Issue for Copilot escalation"
  echo "### ⚠️ Copilot Escalation via Issue (no PR found)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  # GAP-043: Fall back to creating a GitHub Issue so the failure is never silently dropped
  # Write body to a temp file to avoid multi-line string YAML parse issues (actionlint).
  RUN_URL="https://github.com/Aries-Serpent/_codex_/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}"
  printf '@copilot Fix the failing CI workflow **%s** (run [#%s](%s)) on branch `%s`.\n\n' \
    "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" "${RUN_ID}" "${RUN_URL}" "${HEAD_BRANCH}" \
    > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue_body.md"
  printf 'Auto-fix patterns exhausted. Auto-created because no open PR was found.\n\n' \
    >> "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue_body.md"
  printf 'Workflow: %s\nBranch: %s\nRun: %s\nSHA: %s\n\n' \
    "${WORKFLOW_NAME}" "${HEAD_BRANCH}" "${RUN_URL}" "${HEAD_SHA}" \
    >> "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue_body.md"
  printf 'Steps:\n1. Review the failing run linked above\n2. Apply a targeted fix\n3. Push — CI will auto-close this issue on green\n' \
    >> "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue_body.md"
  ISSUE_URL=$(gh issue create \
    --repo Aries-Serpent/_codex_ \
    --title "CI Failure: ${WORKFLOW_NAME} (run #${RUN_ID})" \
    --body-file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/issue_body.md" \
    --label "ci-failure" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$ISSUE_URL" ]; then
    echo "✅ Created escalation issue: ${ISSUE_URL}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  else
    echo "⚠️ Could not create escalation issue (gh CLI unavailable or labels missing)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  fi
  exit 0
fi

RUN_URL="https://github.com/Aries-Serpent/_codex_/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}"

# ── Dedup guard: skip if ANY @copilot rescue/escalation/healing comment
# was posted < 30 min ago — unified across all three posting workflows
# (ci-rescue.yml, iterative-self-healing-ci.yml, copilot-iterative-self-healing.yml).
# Previously each workflow only checked its own marker, allowing all three
# to fire simultaneously for the same failure and each summon the agent
# independently.  The shared check ensures the first poster wins and the
# others are silenced for the 30-minute cooldown window.
ESCALATION_MARKER="<!-- copilot-escalation:${PR_NUMBER} -->"
JQ_EXPR='[.comments[] | select(.body | test("<!-- (ci-rescue-sha|copilot-escalation|copilot-healing):"))] | last | .createdAt // empty'
LAST_ESC=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo Aries-Serpent/_codex_ \
  --json comments --jq "$JQ_EXPR" \
  2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [ -n "$LAST_ESC" ]; then
  NOW_TS=$(date +%s)
  LAST_TS=$(date -d "${LAST_ESC}" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

error_rate_threshold = float(os.environ.get("ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD", "0.05"))

# metric export endpoint; in CI we validate the threshold logic.

    mc.observe("mcp.request.latency_ms", latency_ms)
mc.increment("mcp.request.count", 10)

summary = mc.get_histogram_summary("mcp.request.latency_ms")
total = mc.get_counter("mcp.request.count")
errors = mc.get_counter("mcp.request.error_count")
error_rate = errors / total if total > 0 else 0.0

print(f"Latency summary: count={summary.count} avg={summary.avg_value:.1f}ms "
      f"min={summary.min_value:.1f}ms max={summary.max_value:.1f}ms")
print(f"Request count={total}, error count={errors}, error rate={error_rate:.2%}")

failed = []
if summary and summary.avg_value > latency_threshold:
    failed.append(
        f"mcp.request.latency_ms avg {summary.avg_value:.0f}ms "
        f"> threshold {latency_threshold:.0f}ms"
    )
if error_rate > error_rate_threshold:
    failed.append(
        f"mcp error_rate {error_rate:.2%} "
        f"> threshold {error_rate_threshold:.2%}"
    )

if failed:
    print("❌ MCP metric threshold violations:", file=sys.stderr)
    for f in failed:
